cases.name: Mary K. Schlais
cases.about: “Mary Schlais was more than a victim. She was a brilliant, independent woman, a gifted artist, an equestrian, a world traveler and a scholar,” Nina Mary Schlais, Mary Schlais’ niece, said.
cases.caseStatus: COLD CASE SOLVED; CONVICTION; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED
cases.narrative:
On 2/15/1974, she was found deceased near a wooded intersection of 408th Ave. and 990th St. in the Township of Spring Brook, WI. Police believed she had been hitchhiking from Minneapolis to an art show in Chicago. 

When authorities initially interviewed Miller, they say he denied knowing about Schlais’ killing. When they told him about the DNA evidence they found, Miller admitted to picking her up while she was hitchhiking and asking for “sexual contact.” According to a criminal complaint, when Schlais denied his advances, Miller grabbed a knife he had in his car and stabbed her in the back. An autopsy revealed that she had been stabbed more than a dozen times.
